In addition, in the new circumstances of war and immediate threat of war, everyone had the additional task of being engaged in defence and combat. For the public security station to be able to function, professional policemen, minus Bosniaks now, and minus a number of Serbs who left the station in Vlasenica for the station in Milici, with a very small number remaining, part of the reserve policemen joined active duty policemen in discharging the usual law enforcement duties, including traffic control, and in addition to that, they were also engaged in combat, as required.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the reserve police also participate in manning check-points around Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were check-points at the entry to the town and exit from the town, and reserve policemen were engaged, together with active police, on these check-points as well. But as I've already said, since the number of the active duty force was reduced, then the leader of this mixed team was always an active duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's now turn to the special purpose unit that you mentioned? Could you tell us approximately what the size of that unit was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That unit numbered 20 to 25 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can we take a look at P1044. This is marked for identification earlier this week. It was originally 65 ter 2378. And may we not broadcast this document as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document consists of two lists. If we can look at the first one, it's entitled: "List of Members of the Reserve Police Forces at Vlasenica SJB."

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And perhaps we can go to page 3. I'm sorry, page 3 in the B/C/S, the English, let's stay on page 1. There we go. If we scroll down to the bottom of the B/C/S there's a signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us if that's your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you can go to the very top of the document. This document is not dated but we can see that there's a fax line on it, and it looks like it's July 19, 1992? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I know some time has passed, but would you be able to confirm that generally this is the roster of reserve police around July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These are mainly the policemen who were mobilised and engaged through the Secretariat for National Defence and who were assigned to the station. They would be assigned as regular [as interpreted] policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 4 of the B/C/S and page 2 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, page 58, 20, I believe the witness says, "They would be assigned as reserve policemen," not "regular policemen."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the second list is entitled: "List of members of the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I meant this should be clarified with the witness, I guess. I'm not testifying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: All right. I misunderstood. I thought you thought it was merely a transcription error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in your last answer you said that these reserve policemen were mobilised through the Secretariat of National Defence and were assigned to the station. And then you said: "They would be assigned as" - and the transcript reads - "regular policemen." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I said "reserve policemen."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now this page of the document, the title is list of members of the special platoon at Vlasenica SJB. Is this the special-purpose unit that you were referring to earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page of the B/C/S. Could you tell us whether that is your signature at the bottom of this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we can go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we can look at this list, could you tell us, point out for us who the commander of this special-purpose unit was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miroslav Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall who his -- his Deputy Commanders were from this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I couldn't say with certainty, because I wasn't involved in that part of -- that -- I wasn't involved in that part of the organisation, but I believe Elvis Djuric stood in for him frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about number 8, Zoran Stupar, did he have any leadership role in this unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I know. He was usually in logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just stated that you didn't interact directly with this unit. Who in active police force at SJB Vlasenica would Kraljevic report to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, according to the law and the rule book on internal affairs, the uniformed police is under the command of the police station commander. And according to this hierarchy, he was to report to the commander and receive assignments from the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander at this time, well, at least acting commander was Radenko Stanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While this special-purpose unit was active within the SJB, where would they congregate to receive their daily assignments, either from Kraljevic or from Radenko Stanic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the most part, they were in the combat zone. And if they were not there, then assignments would be made shift by shift. Ten of them or so would be at the ready, at the station. Another group would be on leave, resting. That was the system. So those people who were resting also were duty-bound to report urgently to the station if they were called to go into combat. And they were almost never engaged in police duties because they had no police training or skills whatsoever. And it's perhaps important to note here that this unit used to be an integral part of the so-called special unit attached to the newly established Territorial Defence of Vlasenica. Traditional example -- a classic example of imposition by the Crisis Staff and the leadership is precisely the transfer of this unit to the structure of the ministry. Actually, not transfer, but assigning them to the public security station. And this matter, to the extent that I still had a say at that time, I never definitively approved, and neither did Mr. Bjelanovic. And I believe the minister later reacted in the matter concerning not only this unit but all such units that were attached by various political players in -- in various municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, and I understand you're anxious to explain the situation. But, please, again, address the question that I ask. And just returning to my question, I just want to clarify, when this -- members of this unit would report for assignment to the station, you mean the SJB building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make CSB Chief Cvijetic aware that this unit, this special-purpose unit, existed within SJB Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I met Chief Cvijetic. He was unhappy too, because we were working pursuant to the law. If we needed a reserve policeman, the procedure was well known. We would file a request to the Secretariat for Defence and they would send us men who had at least been military policemen in the former JNA, so they had some prior knowledge and skills. This unit used to be an integral part of the Territorial Defence, and it was resubordinated somewhere in May, around the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify: Resubordinated into the SJB Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned -- well, I am getting from the tenor of your answer that you were not happy about this special unit. Why were you unhappy about them? Were they -- how were they behaving in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, in principle and by law it was not resubordinated as the previous reserve policemen had been resubordinated. When the complement needed to be refilled, when our policemen left for Milici, when we needed replenishment we went through the Secretariat for National Defence, we filed the proper request, we asked for a certain number of people who had prior skills and knowledge and we were given that. However, some time in May or, to be specific, when this Miroslav Kraljevic came to Vlasenica holding himself out to be a lieutenant and when he established this unit as part of the Territorial Defence, the Crisis Staff made the decision that this unit should be seconded or resubordinated or whatever I shall call it to the public security station, circumventing all these procedures that we had insisted on because the ministry required us to. However, we had to go along with it. We had no choice. But we made do somehow, and we directed them exclusively to combat duty, because they had no law enforcement skills.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question -- again, thank you for the explanation, but please focus on the question. My question was: How were they behaving around the town, Vlasenica town, during this time-period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, we had a certain system of work and shifts. You were at the ready, or you were on duty, or you were resting. And they were causing problems around town, disturbing public order and violating the law, and we had no real ability to punish them or hold them accountable in any way. So we sanctioned this conduct as much as we were able.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 23 of this document, is Dragan Nikolic. Is he the same person who was convicted by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May this document be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1044, MFI'd, becomes exhibit under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could take a look at P5 -- strike that. P857. And, again, please do not broadcast this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I have very specific questions to ask you about this document. First of all, does it contain your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In here you report that the special police platoon was formed in Vlasenica SJB in order to realise the goals and on the basis of agreement and suggestions of the Birac SAO government. Can you explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted, trying to draw the minister's attention to the way this unit was seconded, and we were under pressure from the SAO Birac government. Milenko Stanic was the head of that government. And I wanted to draw the minister's attention that the unit was resubordinated in the way that I had already described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do we have the right document on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No, we don't. Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. Perhaps we have the wrong P number, but it's 65 ter 2677. Okay. Now I believe it is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the goals and suggestions of SAO Birac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, look, when you talk about objectives, it's security objectives that are meant. That is unequivocal. And when it says on basis of agreement and suggestions of the Birac Serbian Autonomous District, those were actually pressures to second this unit to the public security station and here is why. The Army of the Republika Srpska had been established by that time, and they tried to foster professionalism just as we did in the ministry so that political leaderships were gradually losing their leverage of influence, and they were trying to hold on to some lever of influence through units like this, and that's why the minister reacted to this problem and asked us to disband such units because they had never been established with his approval, that is, the approval of the ministry of the interior, in the first place, and even for us on the ground they were just a burden because they frequently went out to receive assignments from politicians rather than their immediate superiors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it your position, then, that the special unit was not formed pursuant to the 15 May order of Mico Stanisic? Is that your position now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the order of the 15th of May. The 15 May order is clear. That the existing complement of the police should adjust to the circumstances of the immediate threat of war, that one part of the police force should continue with their law enforcement duties and protect the citizens; whereas, another part of the police should be joined by reserve police to pursue other security and defence duties, including combat. I never had occasion, actually, to talk to the minister, but this unit was like units in -- in some other municipalities. He waited and then issued an order that such units that had been established outside the MUP procedure should be disbanded and that the structure of the ministry should be restored in keeping with the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, pursuant to the minister's instructions you disbanded this special unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pursuant to the minister's instruction, we disbanded, or, rather, reorganised this unit. All the men who had an inclination and met the requirements and wanted to be policemen, were directed by us to an abbreviated police training course. Some others we turned over to the Army of Republika Srpska, and yet another part of these policemen were taken over by the staff of Republika Srpska in Crna Rijeka as security units or something, so that this unit no longer existed as such. Only a couple of young men who really wanted to, who completed the course and who wanted to become policemen, did so; whereas, the others were handed over to the Army of Republika Srpska or the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this letter, you write that the unit was transformed in such way that part of became a reserve contingent. When you wrote "reserve contingent," were you referring to the reserve police or something else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the first stage, those who wanted to remain and who met the criteria, they continued on as reserve policemen, and immediately after that, as soon as the course was set up, they were sent there for training.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could look at 65 ter 2809.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, will this -- will this document be tendered or ... or you don't want to rely on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I believe it's already been admitted into evidence. Perhaps we could have move it to tender it under seal given that the fact that now this witness has identified himself in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it is my recollection that it was called by the 65 ter number, not the exhibit number. That is why I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We have it listed as P857.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the -- it's already exhibited. It just now be placed under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Your Honours. I find out that -- it was my mistake. I'm sorry, Mr. Olmsted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: If we could take look at 65 ter 2809.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're waiting to call this document up, when we -- when you were interviewed last year, you did say that the special unit was created pursuant to this 15 May 1992 order by Mico Stanisic. Why now are you saying that it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't say that it wasn't. Pursuant to the order of the 15th of May, it was necessary to use the existing force as a basis and to replenish it with the reserve force to set up a company, whatever the minister called it, in order to be able to respond to all the challenges, security challenges in the circumstances of war. But I also explained that this unit was attached through the Crisis Staff by the Territorial Defence because it was an integral part of the Territorial Defence of Vlasenica, which was established on the 19th of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can we look at 65 ter 382.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you confirm, is this the order to disband the special units that you were responding to in the previous document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May this document be tendered into -- May this document be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1061, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I want to show you another payroll. It's P1045, marked for identification this week. Its 65 ter number is 2815. And, again, please do not broadcast this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Olmsted, the last document was signed by who? The order to disband the special police units. I don't think we saw the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Yes, I could tell you, for the record, that it's by Zoran Cvijetic. Let me ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who signed that order to disband -- the order that you received to disband the special unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I've already explained this manner of subordination, the minister did co-ordination, and he sent a memo of this kind to the chief of the security centre, and then relayed to him to the public security stations in its original form. I didn't really look, but I think that it was signed by Zoran Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn -- we can stay on page 1 for the English but if we can turn to page 2. And this is a list dated September 1992 of the payroll SJB Vlasenica reserve police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Actually, if you can turn to page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn to the previous page. If we look under number 76 there's Miroslav Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, now let's go back to page 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we see under number 77, Elvis Djuric, and under 97, Dragan Nikolic. Were these -- well, is this some examples of some of the special units members who became members of the reserve police that we just talked about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here we have the names, for instance Kraljevic, Miroslav, was wounded at the time. He was hospitalised. He was wounded some time in August. Which means that at the time when this order was implemented he was there, and probably this is why his name was kept on the list, in order for him to receive his salary. Salaries were not paid regularly. People were paid in arrears and so on. As for Elvis, Djuric, he was a lad who expressed his wish to remain in the reserve force or, rather, to attend the police training course, and that's why he was kept. As for Dragan Nikolic, well, I can't really say whether it was the man or not. I don't think so because he was in the army and he had been in the army at the time before the unit was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could go back to page 2 of the B/C/S. If we look at under number 72 there's a Predrag Basta. Can you tell us are you aware whether this reserve -- can you tell us whether you are aware if this reserve police officer has been convicted of committing war crimes against Muslims in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, the trial ended before a BH court. It was quite recent, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: May we tender this document under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1045 admitted under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just one more payroll I want to show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 2813. And if we could just flip through the pages one after another. I want to see if the witness could authentic these documents, his signature on them. Could you flip to the next page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Can you flip to page 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could you flip to page 7.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: And, finally, page 11.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours I'd like to admit this into evidence as well, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1062, Your Honours. It will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, this will be Exhibit P1062 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We are thinking that in as much as we have five minutes ... she wanted the break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the May through December 1992 time-period, what kinds of uniforms were the reserve police and the special unit wearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm just not clear about what is happening with the part of the transcript that is missing, because I believe the document was admitted and we --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct. I think it was not recorded. 65 ter 2813 is admitted as Exhibit P1062 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Thank you counsel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Back in this May through December 1992 time-period, could you describe for us the uniforms that the reserve and special unit were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Between May and December, depending on the capabilities, well, the uniforms changed. The intent was to have -- for all the police to have the same uniform, camouflage pattern, blue uniform. But in May, June, July, even in August, some of the police officers wore the old style blue MUP uniforms, while the special unit, the one that had been attached, its members came in wearing some kind of camouflage uniforms which were green. It was a makeshift uniform. But based on our requests to the ministry, we did receive a certain number of uniforms, and the active and reserve force, by December, they were all issued with blue camouflage uniforms, and that was the uniform prescribed by law; whereas, the members of the special unit which were involved in combat, the intervention unit, in addition to the blue camouflage uniform, they also had the green camouflage uniform when they went into combat, which means that all the uniforms were harmonised by December. But in this period that you are talking about, various uniforms were in existence, the old style police uniforms, and the camouflage uniforms were gradually phased in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think we can stop there then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, we're about to take the adjournment for today. We will resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. But I am to alert you that having been sworn as a witness you cannot have any communication at all with the lawyers from other side, and in such conversations as you may have with anybody outside of the courtroom, you cannot discuss your testimony. Do you understand what I have said? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we take the adjournment until tomorrow morning.
